providers_reporting_ready.what: what /api/providers/snapshot claims. 'ready' means configured, not logged in: on the isolated E2E server all three answer 'Not logged in'. Read models_that_answered instead.

models_that_answered.what: the model named on stream:end for every send-leg turn. '<synthetic>' or 'none' means no model was called and the run cost nothing. A real model id here means this run spent tokens.

composerToWire.label: Enter -> request leaves the client
composerToWire.what: composer handler, state update and the request body build

wireToAccepted.label: request leaves the client -> the turn exists
wireToAccepted.what: in-flight gate, the SQLite write of the user row, the broadcast and one WebSocket hop back

firstTokenToInk.label: first provider event -> first token readable
firstTokenToInk.what: placeholder bubble, reducer, React and paint

midStreamTokenToInk.label: mid-stream event -> that token readable
midStreamTokenToInk.what: the same path with the bubble already on screen, which is the one that runs hundreds of times a turn

acceptedToFirstProviderEvent.label: accepted -> first provider event
acceptedToFirstProviderEvent.what: time the model and the network take before the first token exists
acceptedToFirstProviderEvent.reason: not measured by construction: the default mode never calls a model, so this leg is absent rather than fast. Re-run with BENCH_AI_REAL=1 against a logged-in provider to measure it. It belongs to the provider and the network and moves for reasons this repo does not control.

request_body_chars.what: size of the POST /api/chat body in UTF-16 code units. The whole transcript used to travel on every turn; today it is a BOUNDED tail, so within one run it still grows message by message and then stops. The invariant is the ceiling (REQUEST_TAIL_BUDGET_CHARS in client/src/hooks/chatRequestPayload.ts), not a constant.

caveats: The four 'ours' intervals are never summed. They are separate paths and two of them overlap in wall clock: the client is already painting its own bubble while the server is still writing the row.
The shell is Chromium (Playwright), not the Tauri WKWebView the product ships. The paint legs are Chromium paint legs.

ink-latency.spec.ts measures a different thing on the same keystroke: Enter until the USER's own message is readable, median 12.4 ms in tests/e2e/ink-budget.json. That bubble is painted optimistically by the client and says nothing about the AI's answer.
